html:
Q'umarkaj, also called Utatlán, was the capital of the K'iche' Maya kingdom in the highlands of Guatemala, founded in the early 1400s. It was burned by the Spanish in 1524.

The K'iche' built a kingdom that ruled much of the highlands, with Q'umarkaj on a plateau ringed by ravines. Its temples, palaces and ball court held the lords of several ruling houses. The Popol Vuh, the sacred book of the K'iche', tells the history of its kings.

When Pedro de Alvarado invaded in 1524, he defeated the K'iche' army, whose hero Tecun Uman died in the battle. Invited into Q'umarkaj, Alvarado suspected a trap, burned the kings alive and destroyed the city. Its rivals, the Kaqchikel, first helped the Spanish but later rose against them. Today little more than mounds remain, still used for Maya rites in Guatemala.
sum: Q'umarkaj, also called Utatlán, was the capital of the K'iche' Maya kingdom in the highlands of Guatemala, founded in the early 1400s. It was burned by the Spanish in 1524.
